consensus_summary: Jacob primarily denotes Israel/the covenant people (names used interchangeably after the renaming) and the archetype of the flawed supplanter transformed by grace into Israel; election and personal spiritual struggle are common secondary readings.
book_summary: Jacob is the crooked, supplanting covenant man or people before God gives the transformed name Israel.
consensus_core_identification: Jacob as Israel/the covenant people and/or the supplanter who becomes Israel
book_core_identification: Jacob as the crooked/supplanting covenant man or people prior to receiving the name Israel
boundary_disagreement: Consensus primary usage treats Jacob as largely synonymous with Israel for the covenant nation (including post-renaming prophetic and NT election language); the book confines the label Jacob to the pre-transformation crooked state and treats Israel as the distinct transformed name.
rationale: Minimum cores share the same referent category: the covenant patriarch/people and the supplanting-to-Israel arc. The book does not replace that referent; it sharpens Jacob specifically to the crooked condition before the Israel name. Consensus already lists the fleshly-Jacob vs. transformed-Israel distinction as a common or minority reading, so the difference is boundary precision (narrowing which cases the name Jacob covers), not core contradiction.
strongest_objection: Biblical and consensus usage often collapses Jacob and Israel as interchangeable names for the covenant nation even after the renaming, so defining Jacob only as the pre-transformation crooked state may over-restrict a synonymy Scripture itself frequently employs.
